pencereler.0-5: Eleven workers died when this oil rig exploded. Then the well burst open, gushing
pencereler.5-12: oil for 87 days. It became the largest marine oil spill in history. But the disaster began with a
pencereler.12-20: test result nobody believed. A pressure test showed gas leaking past the cement seal. Why? The crew misread it as fine and
pencereler.20-30: kept going. When the blowout came, the preventer couldn't cut the bent drill pipe. One bad reading, and one valve that couldn't close.

segmentler.metin: The Deepwater Horizon exploded and sank, spilling oil for 87 days.
It took only a misread negative pressure test.
So how could a misread negative pressure test do this?

The answer is well blowout after a failed cement barrier and a blowout preventer that could not seal — and it is why well-integrity tests and blowout preventers were overhauled under new US offshore safety rules.
